newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland's Merita H1 profit almost triples.
newsitem.headline: Finland's Merita H1 profit almost triples.

text.p: Merita Oy, Finland's largest banking group, on Wednesday said rallying stock markets and falling bad debts had helped produce a surge in first-half profit, eneabling it to meet full-year targets by June.

Reporting operating profit after credit losses at 1.81 billion markka ($324.8 million) against 681 million in the year-ago period, Merita said net loan and guarantee losses were slashed to 325 million from 824 million. ($ = 5.571 Finnish Markka)
"We have achieved the target for the full year already in the first half and see a good development in the second half," a Merita spokeswoman told Reuters.
The result was just over the top of the range of analysts' forecasts in a Reuters poll: they had expected a median around 1.5 billion markka.

Brokers speaking before the Helsinki open said the stock was likely to gain, although perhaps not dramatically with much priced in to a recent rally and a bearish note in U.S. bond markets overnight capping its potential.
"The improvement in performance is attributable in part to the continued decline in expenses and loan losses and an increase in net income from operations," Merita said in its results statement.

"Another contributory factor was a rise in earnings from equity trading, supported by the favourable trend in the stock market." H1 income on securities trading ballooned to 1.35 billion markka net of hedging, up from 552 million.
Merita CEO Vesa Vainio in a statement repeated Merita aimed to pay dividends "which will increase in line with profit".
Merita had earlier said it expected full-year earnings to be distinctly better than in 1996, when it posted a 1.20 billion markka profit on ordinary operations.
